# Yoink

> Free Chrome extension that copies any UI element from any website — HTML, CSS, Tailwind classes, JSX, fonts, asset URLs, screenshots — into an AI-ready bundle for Claude or ChatGPT to reproduce pixel-perfect.

Yoink is a developer/designer tool that lets you hover over any element on any webpage, click to lock it, and copy a complete reproduction package to your clipboard. The package includes a prompt header that instructs an AI model (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, etc.) to recreate the element exactly 1:1, download referenced assets locally, and preserve fonts, hover states, animations, and CSS variables.

## What makes Yoink different

- **AI-first design**: every copy operation includes a built-in prompt that tells the AI to replicate the element exactly, not redesign or "improve" it
- **Deep CSS**: recursive dump of nested children's styles, solving the common "AI got the header wrong because nested CSS was missing" problem
- **Full-page screenshot**: scroll-stitched with sticky-header de-duplication and scrollbar removal
- **Tailwind converter**: maps computed styles to Tailwind v3 utility classes with smart color matching
- **JSX export**: HTML → React JSX with proper camelCase attributes
- **10 localized languages**: EN, RU, ES, ZH, JA, DE, FR, PT, KO, IT

## Pricing

100% free, forever. No paywall, no premium tier, no ads, no accounts. Source-available on GitHub under a proprietary license that permits free use but prohibits modification and redistribution.

## Privacy

No data leaves the user's browser. No servers, no analytics, no telemetry. Only the user's chosen theme, language, and floating-widget position are stored in browser localStorage.

## How it compares

- **vs CSS Peeper / CSS Scan**: Yoink is free and AI-first. CSS Peeper and CSS Scan are paid tools focused on visual inspection without AI integration.
- **vs VisBug**: VisBug is a visual editor. Yoink is an extraction tool — it doesn't edit pages, it copies them for reproduction.
- **vs WhatFont**: WhatFont only identifies fonts. Yoink extracts fonts plus everything else needed to rebuild a component.
- **vs Chrome DevTools**: DevTools requires manual copy-paste of dozens of properties across multiple tabs. Yoink does it in one click with a structured prompt.
